pass_a_gloss: For my people forgot me, they fumed in vain. Indeed every sinner has forgotten God, but the righteous one says: 'All these things have come upon us, and we did not forget you, nor did we act unjustly, and yet you fumed in vain.' But what is to be understood by 'they fumed in vain'? If we take up the things previously said into the 114th Psalm, we shall understand what 'they fumed in vain' means. For in the Psalm it was said thus: 'Let my prayer be set forth as incense before you.' Therefore my prayer is compounded . . . of a refined heart, when our heart is not thickened, it is sent up as incense before God. If then the prayer of the righteous is incense before God, the prayer of the wicked is incense indeed, but of such a sort that it could be said concerning him and the one who makes an unjust prayer: 'They fumed in vain,' as it is written concerning Judas: 'Let his prayer become sin.' And he, while praying, fumed in vain. Who then is the one fuming in vain? Let us understand this still more fully. 'Three times in the year' it says, 'every male of yours shall appear before the Lord your God,' to which is immediately added: 'You shall not appear before me empty.'
